clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside central Turkey

source.quote: Ankara is the capital city of Turkey. Located in the central part of Anatolia, the city has a population of over 5.3 million residents in its urban center, out of 6 million residents in Ankara Province. Ankara is Turkey's second-largest city by population after Istanbul.

clues.text: It sits in one of the driest parts of Turkey, ringed by dry grass steppe. Yet it counts as a green city, with much park land per person.
clues.narrowing: narrows to the dry steppe capital that is paradoxically green

source.quote: Although situated in one of the driest regions of Turkey and surrounded mostly by steppe vegetation (except for the forested areas on the southern periphery), Ankara can be considered a green city in terms of green areas per inhabitant, at 72 square meters (775 square feet) per head.

clues.text: In 1923 it became the new capital of Turkey. It took that role from Istanbul when the old empire fell.
clues.narrowing: shortlists Turkish cities made capital in 1923

source.quote: Ankara became the new Turkish capital upon the establishment of the Republic on 29 October 1923, succeeding the former Ottoman capital Istanbul following the fall of the Ottoman Empire.

clues.text: This city gave its name to soft wool from rabbits. The same name fits a long-haired goat and a fluffy cat.
clues.narrowing: near-decisive: the city named for its wool, goat, and cat

source.quote: The city gave its name to the Angora wool shorn from Angora rabbits, the long-haired Angora goat (the source of mohair), and the Angora cat.

source.quote: Tarija or San Bernardo de la Frontera de Tarixa is a city in southern Bolivia. Founded in 1574, Tarija is the largest city and capital and municipality within the Tarija Department, with an airport offering regular service to primary Bolivian cities, like Bolivia capital La Paz, as well as a regional bus terminal with domestic and international connections.
